outcome: duration of motor and sensory block
time to first postoperative analgesic dose
cohort: 40 ASA I or II parturients scheduled for elective cesarean section
finding: Intrathecal dexmedetomidine provided a longer duration of motor and sensory block compared to intrathecal fentanyl for cesarean section, with similar neonatal outcomes, postoperative analgesia requirements, and maternal satisfaction.
